key_insight: The paper presents a multi-stage post-training pipeline to turn Qwen3.5-27B into a medical LLM using synthetic data curation, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and GRPO-based reward training.
clinical_relevance: This kind of domain adaptation aims to improve the quality and consistency of medical question answering, which could support clinician-facing and educational NLP tools.
method: Synthetic medical data were generated from a MySQL-based knowledge structure, validated by medical PhDs, deduplicated with Chinese RoBERTa, and linguistically refined.
The base model was instruction-tuned with LoRA using MS-Swift, then improved through multi-iteration DPO on 6,283 curated preference pairs.
A parallel GRPO-based reward model used internal rules plus external DeepSeek signals to shape medical response quality.
evidence_signal: Under a uniform LLM-as-Judge evaluation with GPT-5.4, the pipeline reached 77.0% accuracy on MedMCQA and improved mean quality scores from +6.69 at baseline to +7.18 in the final model.
watch_item: The results are reported with LLM-as-Judge and task-specific benchmarks, so real-world clinical reliability, safety, and generalization beyond the evaluated data remain uncertain.
paper_title: Infoxmed2.0-27B: Instruction Tuning, Preference Alignment, and GRPO-Based Reward Model Training for Medical LLMs
